thread.title: Charts: Why Stocks Could Rally After Monday's Beating

title: Charts: Why Stocks Could Rally After Monday's Beating
text:
Charts: Why Stocks Could Rally After Monday's Beating By spy 
I am going to open today with what was good about the market during Monday's decline. Mostly because the fact that the FAANG stocks -- Facebook ( FB ) , Amazon ( AMZN ) , Apple ( AAPL ) , Netflix ( NFLX ) and Alphabet ( GOOGL ) -- finally got sold has many on edge. 
Quite frankly there was very little selling outside of the big cap tech names. And yes I know that is subjective but look at the chart of the Transports and tell me you see selling during Monday's trading session there. I don't. 
If you want to move away from the transports, consider ( JNK ) which we looked at last week because it seemed to be weakening. It did fall on Monday, but it (so far) refused to break the recent lows. 
What is not subjective is the chart of the ( IWM ) relative to the ( SPY ) . It eked out a higher high. That's pretty good news. 
I might also point out that the volume on the QQQs went up quite a bit which typically means a short-term rally. I do need to note however that the gap down on Monday morning left an island overhead so if we do get a short-term rally and it fails to fill that gap overhead that is bearish because islands at tops are bearish. 
Okay, I'm done with the good news. You will notice that my Oscillator is still quite overbought. I understand that breadth has been negative for four of the last five trading days. But I can't change the fact that over the next five trading days there is not one negative number to be dropped off the 10-day moving average of the advance/decline line (the input for the Oscillator). I can't make it get oversold until we are staring at dropping negative numbers ahead of us, and that just won't happen in the next few days. 
I even went back to look if the Nasdaq Momentum Indicator, which is based on price, not breadth, would see an oversold condition quickly. The earliest I can find one there is near Friday of this week. 
I also can't change the fact that the 30-day moving average of the advance/decline line stops dropping red numbers this week. That makes it overbought as well. 
Then there's that 50-day moving average looming overhead. We've discussed the DJIA but now that the S&P 500 has come back under it, that 2740-2750 area overhead looms as resistance. 
And what of sentiment? The chatter I saw sounded concerned, much more concerned than it was a week ago. But the put/call ratio was 102% which speaks of some elevated caution but not the kind of fear you'd expect from the kind of day we saw. 
I will end with what I have said for the last few days. I think we can rally but I don't think we can go very far until we get back to an oversold condition.
